title: Natural Selection plays no necessary part in producing spiral shell forms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural Selection plays no necessary part in producing spiral shell forms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Natural Selection, in any strictly biological sense, has no necessary share in producing the varied forms of spiral shells, which arise from differences in growth rates and ratios.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is hard indeed (to my mind) to see where Natural Selection necessarily enters in, or to admit that it has had any share whatsoever in the production of these varied conformations.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Shell forms and Natural Selection”. Scope: spiral shells of molluscs, foraminifera and worms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing data can test whether selection is associated with shell form and whether growth laws generate observed possibilities. They cannot resolve the non-necessity formulation cleanly, because a physical growth mechanism does not exclude evolutionary selection on its parameters.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare generative growth-only models and selection-aware evolutionary models against shell-form distributions, fitness proxies and phylogenetic transitions. Growth laws explain possibility, while evidence that form affects survival or reproduction would refute the strongest claim of no selective share.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil occurrence is an imperfect fitness proxy.

Growth constraints and natural selection are compatible rather than exclusive.

'No necessary share' is a modal claim and cannot be proved by observational fit.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim denies that natural selection, in a strictly biological sense, is needed to produce spiral shell diversity, while granting that the forms follow from growth rates. Shell morphospaces can describe those rates and cannot show that selection was unnecessary in producing them. Every plausible distribution of forms fits both the claim and its rival, so the denial has no separating empirical consequence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No measurement of shell form distinguishes growth ratios that made selection unnecessary from growth ratios that selection had already shaped. Showing that coiling follows from growth ratios restates the geometry and does not test whether selection had a necessary share.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Any observed set of growth ratios is compatible both with selection on those ratios and with selection playing no necessary part.

Widening natural selection to any filter that makes some forms common, as the text itself notes, removes the biological contrast.
